open_points.subject: content-derived identities
open_points.text: Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)
open_points.question: How are edges or constants ordered for hashing when their stated sort keys are equal but their remaining content differs?
options: Add a total tie-breaker using all canonical content
Preserve submission order for tied items
Refuse repeated sort keys at composition
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical JSON of the complete item as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: proof failure ordering
open_points.text: both ports exist with the right direction; both carry the same schema, the same carriage and, for files, the same media type
open_points.question: When several endpoint conditions fail on one edge, what exact source-versus-target and existence-versus-direction order determines the reported first reason?
options: Source existence, source direction, target existence, target direction
Check both exist before either direction
Target checks before source checks
open_points.default_guess: Check source existence and direction, then target existence and direction, followed by schema, carriage and media type.

open_points.subject: proof ordering for tied edges
open_points.text: edges, by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`)
open_points.question: If two distinct edges have the same four endpoint fields, what orders them when their guards differ and one fails before the other?
options: Order by guard port and guard value after the endpoint fields
Treat them as the same proof item
Refuse duplicate endpoint tuples before proof
open_points.default_guess: Extend the edge order with the canonical guard content.

open_points.subject: redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: is returned to an agent only as its length and that class
open_points.question: Is the disclosed failure-detail length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes, or the original untruncated text?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the stored bounded detail
Unicode scalar values of the stored detail
Length of the original detail before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, truncated detail.

open_points.subject: clock prohibition in the sandbox
open_points.text: The replaced entry points are exactly: `time.time`, `time.time_ns`, `time.monotonic`, `time.monotonic_ns`, `time.perf_counter`, `time.perf_counter_ns`, `time.process_time`, `time.process_time_ns`, `time.localtime`, `time.gmtime`, `time.ctime` and `time.asctime` when called without an argument
open_points.question: Are other CPython 3.12 clock-reading entry points, such as `time.clock_gettime`, `time.clock_gettime_ns`, `time.thread_time`, `time.thread_time_ns` and `os.times`, allowed or sandbox violations?
options: Allow every clock API not in the closed list
Trap every clock-reading API and expand the release list
Remove the absolute no-clock guarantee and guarantee only the listed traps
open_points.default_guess: Trap every clock-reading API and expand the closed release list.

open_points.subject: determinism of function executions
open_points.text: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
open_points.question: How is this guarantee enforced for Python code that can observe process identity, object addresses, thread scheduling, filesystem enumeration or other nondeterministic state not covered by the listed traps?
options: Forbid and trap every remaining nondeterministic observation
Permit nondeterministic code and remove the guaranteed equal digest
Execute repeatedly and refuse implementations whose outputs differ
open_points.default_guess: Treat the guarantee as admission-relevant and refuse implementations when repeated executions differ.

open_points.subject: sandbox wall-time interval
open_points.text: ResourceBounds M04 are enforced from outside the environment with ... the parent's own wall deadline
open_points.question: At what event does `wall_time_ms` begin and end: environment creation, interpreter start, module loading, entry to `run`, return from `run`, or completed cleanup?
options: From sandbox process start through process exit
From entry to `run` through its return
From environment creation through confirmed cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Measure from sandbox process start until the function process exits, with cleanup governed separately by rule 7.

open_points.subject: capture of a mapped function failure
open_points.text: A mapped node ... calls `run` once per element with that element in place of the mapped port's list. / It copies its inputs ... into the case as values and file fixtures.
open_points.question: When a failed mapped execution received one element in place of a contract port whose cardinality is `many`, what becomes the TrialCase input so that it fits the contract port?
options: Wrap the element in a one-element list
Capture the original full mapped list
Refuse capture of mapped-element executions
open_points.default_guess: Wrap the failed element in a one-element list for the mapped input port.

open_points.subject: rollback eligibility
open_points.text: Rollback activates an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract version
open_points.question: What exactly makes an implementation “earlier,” especially after a rollback: submission order, activation order, or merely being a non-current existing implementation?
options: Any non-current implementation with a current-corpus admitted verdict
Only an implementation submitted before the current implementation
Only an implementation appearing in an earlier activation
open_points.default_guess: Allow any non-current implementation of that contract version with an admitted verdict for the current corpus.

open_points.subject: credential control characters
open_points.text: holds an empty value or a control character
open_points.question: Which code points count as control characters in a credential value?
options: ASCII C0 characters plus DEL
All Unicode General Category Cc characters
All Unicode control and format characters
open_points.default_guess: Reject ASCII U+0000–U+001F and U+007F after removing one trailing LF.

open_points.subject: encoded credential disclosure
open_points.text: Secrets ... never enter ... an answer. / one that carries it in another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class
open_points.question: May a service response containing an encoded form of a credential be returned as an `open` or `business_confidential` value, despite State 0 saying secrets never enter an answer?
options: Never return recognizable encoded credentials
Return them according to the binding's disclosure class
Treat the State 0 promise as applying only to verbatim credentials
open_points.default_guess: Treat only verbatim credential bytes as detectable and narrow the State 0 promise accordingly.

open_points.subject: data-directory privacy
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission checks define “private,” and are parent directories, SQLite side files and newly created files included?
options: Kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission on every object under the data directory
Check only the data-directory mode
Require fixed modes such as 0700 for directories and 0600 for files, including side files
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission on the directory and every contained object, including SQLite side files.

open_points.subject: oversized non-2xx service responses
open_points.text: Over a ceiling is always a refusal or a failure, never a truncation — for code, values, files, requests, responses and outputs. / status 3xx or 5xx, whatever the body's size — reading stops at the ceiling
open_points.question: Does an oversized 3xx, 4xx or 5xx response keep its status-derived outcome after the body is truncated, or does exceeding `service_response_bytes_max` produce a distinct failure?
options: Keep the status-derived outcome and truncate only diagnostic capture
Treat every oversized response as a ceiling failure
Read and discard the complete body before deciding
open_points.default_guess: Keep the status-derived outcome and define the ceiling as a read/discard limit for unused error bodies, explicitly exempting them from A20's no-truncation rule.

open_points.subject: release-pinned dependencies
open_points.text: one release fixes every ceiling and every dependency / the kernel checks at start ... that `bubblewrap` is present and that one probe execution succeeds
open_points.question: Must the release pin and verify an exact `bubblewrap` version, or may any host version that passes the probe serve as the security boundary?
options: Pin and verify an exact bubblewrap version
Accept any bubblewrap version that passes the probe
Declare bubblewrap a host prerequisite outside the release dependency guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Pin and verify the exact bubblewrap version as part of the release.

open_points.subject: empty mapped file outputs
open_points.text: A mapped node over an empty list ... writes one NodeExecution `succeeded` ... with every output an empty list. / a file list is the elements' SpooledFiles ... An empty list is named, with its class, by the one NodeExecution
open_points.question: How does a NodeExecution represent and type an empty `many` file output when there are no SpooledFile facts and M23 permits only StoredValue or SpooledFile references?
options: Add an explicit empty-file-list reference carrying class and media type
Represent it as an empty array directly in the NodeExecution
Use a StoredValue even though run files are otherwise never StoredValues
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit empty-file-list reference carrying its class, media type and cardinality.

open_points.subject: oversized mapped output among several outputs
open_points.text: a list whose canonical bytes exceed `stored_value_bytes_max` is not written: the node is then failed for its dependants
open_points.question: If one mapped output list is within the ceiling and another is over it, are any valid lists delivered or exposed as run outputs before the node is treated as failed?
options: Deliver none of the mapped node's outputs
Deliver valid output lists while failing only dependants of the oversized output
Delivery depends on output-port order
open_points.default_guess: Validate every delivered output list first and deliver none if any required list exceeds the ceiling.

open_points.subject: resolution of an unknown outcome
open_points.text: `service_unreachable` and `outcome_unknown` are waits, not failures, and their dependants wait, until the owner's resolution makes the element count as succeeded or failed / `not_applied`: the element waits again with reason `owner_approval`
open_points.question: After resolving an unknown attempt as `not_applied`, is the element concluded as failed or does it remain unconcluded and waiting for a fresh approval?
options: Remain unconcluded and wait for a fresh approval
Conclude failed immediately
Conclude the old attempt failed while creating a distinct pending resend element
open_points.default_guess: Keep the element unconcluded and waiting for the fresh approval, as A11 rule 3 specifies.

open_points.subject: manifest structural errors
open_points.text: the service record is absent, is not valid JSON, lacks `service` or `capabilities`, or its `service` field differs
open_points.question: Which manifest-mismatch reason and precedence apply when fields are present with the wrong JSON type, capability entries are not objects, names are missing or non-strings, or canonicalization is impossible because of duplicate object keys?
options: Treat all such cases as invalid JSON
Define ordered structural manifest checks before semantic checks
Treat the operation as absent whenever its entries cannot be searched
open_points.default_guess: Define ordered structural checks and classify duplicate keys or non-canonicalizable JSON as invalid JSON.

open_points.subject: missing idempotency_key member
open_points.text: The idempotency key fields are read from the entry's `idempotency_key`: `null` means none; otherwise the text split on `+`
open_points.question: What happens when the capability entry omits `idempotency_key`, or supplies a non-null non-string value?
options: Treat an omitted member as `null` and refuse non-string values
Require the member and refuse omission
Refuse both omission and every non-string value
open_points.default_guess: Treat omission as `null` and refuse non-null values that are not strings.

open_points.subject: api_base_url grammar
open_points.text: one that is not an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host counts as none
open_points.question: Are user-info, a query, a fragment, or a non-root path allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they combined with the operation path and represented in the Host header?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port
Allow a path prefix but forbid user-info, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL and apply standard URL resolution
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, host, optional port and an optional path prefix; forbid user-info, query and fragment.

open_points.subject: multipart port names
open_points.text: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part
open_points.question: What happens when a port name contains a quote, backslash, CR, LF, non-ASCII text or another character requiring Content-Disposition escaping?
options: Restrict port names to a safe ASCII field-name grammar
Define exact quoted-string escaping and encoding
Percent-encode multipart names and filenames
open_points.default_guess: Restrict port names used in multipart requests to a safe ASCII identifier grammar at binding proposal.

open_points.subject: service response byte ceiling
open_points.text: The status line and headers are read up to `service_response_bytes_max` bytes together / the body exceeds `service_response_bytes_max`
open_points.question: Is `service_response_bytes_max` one limit for the entire response or two independent limits, one for status-plus-headers and another for the body?
options: One combined response limit
Separate full-size limits for header section and body
A separate unstated header limit plus the stated body limit
open_points.default_guess: Use one combined limit for status line, headers and decoded body.

open_points.subject: incomplete response body
open_points.text: request may have been sent, no valid final response received (timeout, reset, EOF, a malformed status line or headers, only `1xx`) / status 2xx ... outputs do not fit rule 3
open_points.question: If valid final status and headers arrive but the body times out, resets or ends prematurely, is that “no valid final response” and therefore unknown, or a status-derived applied/not-applied outcome with invalid outputs?
options: Treat every incomplete body as no valid final response
Use the final status to decide applied or not-applied despite the incomplete body
Use status only for responses whose framing completed
open_points.default_guess: Treat an incompletely framed body as no valid final response and therefore `outcome_unknown` for a non-read operation.

open_points.subject: multipart boundary collision
open_points.text: the boundary ... is the kernel's framing of the parts the owner was shown
open_points.question: How must the kernel choose or retry a multipart boundary when the chosen delimiter occurs in a part's bytes?
options: Generate and check boundaries until none collides with any part
Use a deterministic boundary derived from all part digests and reject a collision
Rely on a random boundary without checking
open_points.default_guess: Generate a boundary and verify that it does not collide with any part before sending.

open_points.subject: seeded pseudorandomness
open_points.text: no ... randomness / `random.Random(seed)` with an explicit seed stays usable
open_points.question: Does State 0 prohibit all random-number APIs, including deterministic seeded pseudorandom generation, or only access to nondeterministic entropy?
options: Prohibit every random-number API
Allow deterministic seeded pseudorandom generation
Allow it only when the seed is derived solely from inputs
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the prohibition as excluding nondeterministic entropy and allow explicitly seeded generators.

open_points.subject: function filesystem access
open_points.text: no filesystem beyond its input / an audit hook that raises ... on opening any path outside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime
open_points.question: May function code read arbitrary files in the read-only runtime and read or write arbitrary paths in the exchange directory, or may it access only its declared input and output artifacts?
options: Permit access anywhere in the mounted runtime and exchange directory
Expose only declared input and output paths
Permit runtime reads but restrict exchange access to declared artifacts
open_points.default_guess: Permit runtime reads required for imports but restrict exchange-directory access to declared input and output artifacts.
